evidence.quote:
As Moher et al. concede, “time and resource constraints …
limited inclusion of perspectives of other relevant groups (e.g.
authors, readers, peer reviewers)” in developing the CC3. We
believe input from authors is fundamental to efforts to define
competencies of journal editors, and suggest that insights into
authors’ (sometimes less than satisfactory) experiences with
journals can be provided by another type of editor, namely
authors’ editors4–10. These editors help researcher-authors prepare
manuscripts for publication by reading drafts and suggesting
changes to structure and content (substantive editing), language

and style (language editing), and appearance and format (e.g. compliance with journals’ instructions)9,11. In addition, many authors’
editors train researchers in publication skills12–17 and help authors
navigate editorial processes18–21. Authors’ editors’ knowledge
of the publication process and their close interactions with the
producers, distributors and consumers of research information
make them qualified to help define CC for journal editors and
identify deficiencies in current practices8.

Authors’ editors are often more familiar with researchers’ local
circumstances and challenges than journal editors are. Although
the writers of the consensus statement and their informants are
themselves researchers and therefore authors, they were perhaps
not representative of the wider population of “real-world”
researchers who have limited contact with English-speaking
opinion leaders in biomedical publishing. In contrast, many
authors’ editors work with researchers whose first language is
not English or who are based outside the global North and West.
Familiarity with other languages and cultures gives authors’ editors
insights into the types of competencies researchers from diverse
geographical, cultural and linguistic backgrounds would value in
journal editors.
Like journal editors, authors’ editors are taking steps to critically
evaluate and improve their working methods. A growing body of
literature9 facilitates knowledge transfer to colleagues in different
settings. PhD degrees have been awarded to authors’ editors for
applied linguistics research based on their work practices in the
Netherlands22, Spain23 and China (Luo24 and unpublished; available
upon request). Continuing professional development for authors’
editors is available through national and international associations
(Table 1). Authors’ editors in these associations can provide
valuable information about journal editor CC that researchers
would value. As authors’ editors ourselves, we offer suggestions on
how to improve the CC based on insights we and our colleagues
gain about researchers’ experiences with peer review.

In our experience, reviewers and journal editors increasingly cite
“problems with the English” as a reason for rejection, even of
manuscripts free from language errors. Meanwhile, biomedical journals publish an ever-increasing proportion of articles that
were judged by reviewers to have “acceptable English” but which
contain awkwardly worded statements that defy comprehension
and undermine reproducibility9(pp5–9). To avoid these problems,
journal editors should be able to either provide authors with
useful feedback on the language (e.g. by endorsing or overruling
reviewers’ complaints) or delegate this responsibility to an
appropriately skilled reviewer or editorial staffer. Relying solely
on blanket “acceptable/unacceptable” assessments of the writing
contributes, in our experience, to cynicism among authors
regarding the fairness and quality of peer review, and to the
proliferation of poorly written articles. Although we realize that
skills in “dealing with language issues” and knowledge about the
“fundamentals of editing” were considered but then excluded from
the CC2, we believe that inclusion of a competency in this area
would be welcomed and perceived as a marker of editorial quality.

Another competency researchers would appreciate is the ability
of journal editors to deal effectively with inappropriate text
re-use. This omission from the CC is surprising, especially since
plagiarism featured in two of the 23 highly ranked statements in
the Delphi process2. While working with authors on manuscripts,
authors’ editors sometimes encounter re-used text and inadequate
citation, and use these opportunities to explain why these
practices may be inappropriate and how to avoid them25. But
these individual efforts are not enough to stop the global spread of
plagiarism in published research, which journal editors may inadvertently facilitate if they do not check manuscripts carefully
enough before publication. Journal editors should be able to
interpret the results of “plagiarism-detection” software and deal
sensitively with the manuscripts these tools single out (as proposed by the Committee on Publications Ethics, publicationethics.
org/files/u2/02A_Plagiarism_Submitted.pdf). Setting a maximum

allowable percentage of text overlap, without considering the
context of the non-original text, may send inconsistent messages
about appropriate and inappropriate text re-use. Manuscript
rejection based solely on the percentage of non-original text can,
in our experience, alienate well-meaning authors from journals that
use this criterion.

Competing interests
VM and KS are both self-employed authors’ editors and realize
that this article might attract clients. VM is the author of the
book Editing Research and realizes that this article might affect
sales. VM and KS are both long-time members of Mediterranean
Editors and Translators, and have been unpaid speakers at
CPD events run by this organization. KS was Vice Chair of
Mediterranean Editors and Translators during 2006. KS is a
long-time member of Asetrad and was an unpaid speaker at a
CPD event run by this organization in 2017.

reference_points.judgment: 纳入作者编辑的经验可补充决策编辑视角，但作者编辑不能自动代表所有作者，职业协会/博士及继续教育例子亦不能推出全行业具有统一资格或能力。
reference_points.importance_reason: 关系利益相关者代表性与能力主张的范围。
acceptable_alternatives: 可以认可其作为补充咨询来源，无需要求概率抽样；建议明确专业能力异质性而非否定职业贡献。

reference_points.judgment: 作者提出语言反馈与处理文本复用两项可识别能力，并区分支持/否决审稿语言评价、适当授权及重合百分比与情境判断；宜进一步说明能力如何落实和评估。
reference_points.importance_reason: 建议具有操作起点，但能力清单仍需具体表现标准。
acceptable_alternatives: 不必要求在短篇通信中建立完整培训量表；转介合适服务、公开写作判据可作为可选建设性延伸。

reference_points.judgment: 英文问题拒稿增多、难读论文比例不断增长及拒稿导致疏离等经验概括，应保留“in our experience”限定或补证据，不可直接推广总体趋势。
reference_points.importance_reason: 经验来源能提出议题，但不足以估计普遍趋势与因果效果。
acceptable_alternatives: 可接受经验性评论的措辞，前提是不将其当定量调查结论；无需新增大规模研究才有发表价值。

reference_points.judgment: 作者已充分披露自雇编辑、潜在客户和书籍收益及协会关系；应评估利益位置影响论证，不能声称未披露或据商业利益判建议无效。
reference_points.importance_reason: 保证评论公允，并区分利益披露与证据评价。
acceptable_alternatives: 允许要求反映不同作者群体的独立意见，但不得以披露的利益自动否定内容。

evidence_accuracy.focus: 正确复述两项能力、作者编辑角色、现有引文和利益披露。
high_score_conditions: 准确区分经验陈述与规范建议，指出原稿已有详尽利益披露。
核心意见均由原稿精确文字支持，不虚构研究数据、通用资格或未披露冲突。
low_score_risks: 声称百分比重合等于抄袭

levels.0: 核心证据捏造、对象/版本颠倒或与题内材料直接矛盾，导致主要判断失效。 确认有效作答尝试但无实质回答时该维记0，并标记nonresponse。运行失败或材料不足本身不按0处理；有依据地限定判断仍可高分。
levels.1: 引用零散或错配，主要判断缺少可定位支持；把作者声称当已核事实。
levels.2: 识别部分问题但遗漏重要边界：须承认已披露利益并分清能力建议与实证趋势。
levels.3: 准确区分经验陈述与规范建议，指出原稿已有详尽利益披露。
levels.4: 核心意见均由原稿精确文字支持，不虚构研究数据、通用资格或未披露冲突。

evidence_accuracy.boundary_2_3: 须承认已披露利益并分清能力建议与实证趋势。
evidence_accuracy.boundary_3_4: 同时覆盖角色范围和两项能力，而非只抓一个职业资质意见。

argument_validity.focus: 职业经验为何可补充利益相关者意见，以及能力主张的操作与证据边界。
high_score_conditions: 把资质异质性、代表性和经验概括各自联系到结论范围。
能提出可行澄清/操作化建议，并承认短篇通信可提出规范倡议，无需硬加实验。
low_score_risks: 以职业利益作人身式否定
要求短通信必须做因果实验

levels.0: 主要推论无效或依赖错误科学前提，无法支撑判断。 确认有效作答尝试但无实质回答时该维记0，并标记nonresponse。运行失败或材料不足本身不按0处理；有依据地限定判断仍可高分。
levels.1: 主要靠断言、权威/平台状态或服从评审；未建立证据到判断的关系。
levels.2: 识别部分问题但遗漏重要边界：由泛称缺数据提升为指出哪项趋势或代表性推论超出依据。
levels.3: 把资质异质性、代表性和经验概括各自联系到结论范围。
levels.4: 能提出可行澄清/操作化建议，并承认短篇通信可提出规范倡议，无需硬加实验。

argument_validity.boundary_2_3: 由泛称缺数据提升为指出哪项趋势或代表性推论超出依据。
argument_validity.boundary_3_4: 允许合理赞同与新有效意见；不把真人推荐转介当唯一正确要求。

conclusion_appropriateness.focus: 认可评论价值但不宣称建议已证明改善科研质量。
high_score_conditions: 对能力拓展提出有条件支持，区分经验性倡议与效果证据。
总体评价与实质问题权重一致，保留规范文体定位，不夸大局部局限为全篇无效。
low_score_risks: 以同行赞同或平台批准证明正确

levels.0: 总判断与已核关键证据相反或严重越过任务可知范围。 确认有效作答尝试但无实质回答时该维记0，并标记nonresponse。运行失败或材料不足本身不按0处理；有依据地限定判断仍可高分。
levels.1: 结论过度确定/泛化，忽略决定性缺口，或用拒绝作答回避可判断部分。
levels.2: 识别部分问题但遗漏重要边界：不能将两项经验主张未普遍验证推成全部建议无价值。
levels.3: 对能力拓展提出有条件支持，区分经验性倡议与效果证据。
levels.4: 总体评价与实质问题权重一致，保留规范文体定位，不夸大局部局限为全篇无效。

conclusion_appropriateness.boundary_2_3: 不能将两项经验主张未普遍验证推成全部建议无价值。
conclusion_appropriateness.boundary_3_4: 把主要修订需求与可选未来验证区分。

severe_error_checks: 不把作者编辑当作者群体的自动代表
不把文本复用与剽窃一概等同
不指控不存在的利益未披露

read: 完整读取本题提取文本，含正文、表1文本、利益披露与参考文献；先前完整读取两份当轮报告及答复仅作为候选问题线索。
not_read: 未目视表1原图；未核验协会信息或引文原作。
verification_limits: 不声称表格视觉校验或趋势事实外部验证；评分依据本题原稿。

concern_coverage.finding: 原稿已有授权适当编辑反馈，没有明确转介服务，属于可行延伸

concern_coverage.concern: R2资质/核心能力与继续教育异质性
concern_coverage.finding: 原稿以协会/博士和专业互动支持职业贡献，需限制代表性与同质性暗示
报告主体赞同语言反馈和文本复用能力，不能把每段赞扬当新增要求
